# Things not to do

Short list of Python habits that look flexible but usually make code harder to read,
refactor, and debug. Each item is a **footgun** — fine in libraries with a narrow
purpose, costly in application and research code. See [Useful Patterns](useful-patterns.qmd#useful-patterns) for the constructive counterpart.

Future entries will use the same red callout style as [Geometry and collision](geometry-and-collision.qmd#geometry-and-collision).

## `*args` and `**kwargs` without a reason

`*args` and `**kwargs` collect extra positional and keyword arguments into a tuple
and dict. They exist so **wrappers can forward** to another function when the
signature is intentionally open ([PEP 3102](https://peps.python.org/pep-3102/),
[`*args` / `**kwargs` in the tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/controlflow.html#more-on-defining-functions)).

They are **not** a substitute for naming what your function actually takes.

### Bad — “flexible” API, unclear contract

```python
def train(*args, **kwargs):
    return run_loop(*args, **kwargs)


def set_joint_targets(*args, **kwargs):
    # Which argument is q_des? Which actuator? kwargs keys undefined.
    ...
```

Problems:

- Call sites do not document intent — `train(1e-3, 500, True)` is opaque.
- The editor cannot autocomplete parameter names or catch `damping="1e-3"` (string).
- Refactor-rename (`epochs` → `max_steps`) misses stringly call sites; grep is noisy.
- The next reader must read the whole body (or every caller) to learn the API.

[Do not add `*args` / `**kwargs` to ordinary functions “for future flexibility.” Name the parameters you support today; add new ones explicitly when needed. Reserve variadic signatures for true forwarders (decorators, thin adapters) or APIs that mirror an underlying variadic hook.]{.common-bug-warning}

### Better — explicit parameters

```python
def train(*, learning_rate: float, max_steps: int, log: bool = False) -> None:
    run_loop(learning_rate=learning_rate, max_steps=max_steps, log=log)


def set_joint_targets(data, q_des: np.ndarray, actuator_ids: list[int]) -> None:
    for act_id, q in zip(actuator_ids, q_des, strict=True):
        data.ctrl[act_id] = q
```

Keyword-only parameters (`*` before names) still prevent positional drift at the
call site without hiding names.

### When variadic signatures *are* reasonable

| Pattern | Example in this repo |
|---|---|
| Decorator forwards to wrapped function | `@timed` in [Useful Patterns — decorators](useful-patterns.qmd#decorators) (`wrapped(*args, **kwargs)`) |
| Registry / factory passes options through | `make_ik("dls", damping=1e-2)` — kwargs match **one** constructor, documented on the class |
| Subclass hook matching a base signature | Rare in our code; still document allowed keys |

Rule of thumb: if **you** are the author of the callee and callers are **your**
 teammates, prefer explicit names. If you are writing a **one-line forwarder** to
 code you do not control, `*args` / `**kwargs` is idiomatic.
